summary:
We developed Flame Atlas, an uncertainty-aware spacecraft and planetary fire-safety digital twin powered by NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) datasets (`BASS-II`, `SAFFIRE-II`, `FLEX`, `SAME`, `SPICE`, and `ACME CFI-G`). The web dashboard pairs a Gaussian Process surrogate model and inverse design optimizer with a 60 FPS parametric flame visualizer and automated NASA investigation ranker.

Engineers can simulate ignition-to-burndown flame size, color, spread rate, and safe object movement speeds across 14 Solar System bodies, surface altitudes, cabin oxygen concentrations, and spacecraft materials. Rather than acting as a black box, our AI Trust Meter and visual uncertainty halo warn designers when predictions extrapolate into unverified partial-gravity or high-oxygen regimes, while recommending material swaps, dust-immune smoke detection, and suppression protocols.

As humanity returns to the Moon and Mars in elevated-oxygen habitats where buoyancy is reduced and cool flames burn nearly invisible, knowing when an AI model is uncertain protects astronaut lives—while translating NASA microgravity research into terrestrial cleanroom detectors and fine-water-mist suppression.
details:
Flame Atlas — Uncertainty-Aware Spacecraft & Planetary Fire-Safety Digital Twin

WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

Flame Atlas transforms NASA's 12-terabyte Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion archive into an interactive, uncertainty-aware engineering atlas for spacecraft, lunar bases, and planetary habitats. Rather than forcing engineers to dig through fragmented spreadsheets and multi-gigabyte high-speed video logs, Flame Atlas combines a Gaussian Process surrogate model, an ambient AI engineering engine, and a 60 FPS parametric HTML5 Canvas flame digital twin on a single mission-control dashboard:

* Solar System & Altitude Gravity Engine: Users select any of 14 Solar System bodies (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Moon, Mars, Ceres, Jupiter, Europa, Ganymede, Titan, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto), toggle Orbital Freefall ($0g$), and adjust altitude above the surface ($h$) to compute exact local gravity via:

$$g(h) = g_0 \left(\frac{R}{R + h}\right)^2$$

* Data-Driven Ignition-to-Burndown Flame Visualizer: Driven directly by empirical NASA PSI parameters—never random Earth-style CGI—the visualizer simulates the three-phase combustion timeline: initial ignition vapor flare ($t = 0$), diffusion relaxation, and steady propagation or $d^2$-law droplet decay. It renders calibrated standoff gaps, blue chemiluminescence vs. yellow soot color gradients, melting PMMA bubble-ejection streaks, and round-to-teardrop elongation based on object movement speed and direction ($\vec{v}_{\text{rel}} = \vec{v}_{\text{vent}} - \vec{v}_{\text{obj}}$).

* Safe Movement Speed Range Gauge: Using ISS wind-tunnel data, Flame Atlas calculates the exact Quench Limit, Danger Flare-Up Band, and Blow-Off Velocity so crew and engineers know the safe speed limits for moving burning or heated materials.

* AI Trust Meter & Visual Uncertainty Halo: Every prediction displays a translucent, dashed $\pm 95\%$ confidence halo around the flame and a real-time Trust Gauge (HIGH_CONFIDENCE, CAUTION_EXTRAPOLATING, or UNVERIFIED_REGIME_DO_NOT_TRUST) that warns engineers when they enter uncharted regimes (such as lunar $1/6g$ gravity at elevated oxygen levels).

* Ambient AI Engineering Modules (No Generic Chatbot):

- Inverse Design Optimizer ("Find Me a Safe Setup"): Locks fixed mission constraints (e.g., Lunar $32\%\text{ O}_2$ at $10.2\text{ psi}$) and searches across materials, airflows, and carry speeds to output 3 one-click safe configurations while respecting human breathability limits ($\text{ppO}_2 \ge 2.9\text{ psi}$).

- Regime-Shift Interpreter & Cliff-Edge Scanner: Automatically explains why flame geometry or confidence shifts when crossing physical boundaries and flags nearby non-linear flare-up or invisible cool-flame thresholds.

- NASA PSI Investigation Ranker & Safety Playbook: Ranks the Top 4 matching NASA experiments with similarity scores, parameter diffs, DOI links, and actionable Prevention (material swaps), Detection (smoke vs. lunar dust false-alarm thresholds and invisible flame alerts), and Suppression ($\text{CO}_2$/$\text{He}$ dilution and HVAC cutoff protocols) guidance.

---

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

* De-Risking Lunar & Martian Habitats: Future Artemis lunar bases and pressurized rovers will use elevated oxygen (greater than $30\%$) and reduced pressure (less than $10.2\text{ psi}$) to shorten spacesuit pre-breathe times—dramatically increasing flammability in a partial-gravity regime where zero flight combustion data currently exists. Flame Atlas prevents over-reliance on AI predictions by quantifying extrapolation uncertainty and recommending conservative engineering safety margins.

* Accelerating Research Discovery: Cuts hours of manual cross-referencing across NASA hardware racks (CIR, MSG, MDCA, Cygnus) down to milliseconds, linking every prediction directly to published NASA datasets and DOIs.

* Terrestrial Fire-Safety Spinoffs: A dedicated Earth Spinoff Impact Banner translates microgravity findings into practical Earth applications—including fine-water-mist fire extinguishers, semiconductor cleanroom and aircraft cargo smoke detectors (distinguishing dust from smoldering wire aerosols), and firefighter protective gear.

---

HOW FLAME ATLAS IS CREATIVE

* Honest Safety-Critical AI: Most predictive tools display single point estimates that encourage false confidence. Making epistemic uncertainty a physical, visual boundary (an expanding dashed halo around the flame) aligns AI design with real aerospace safety engineering.

* Galilean Movement Mapping: By mapping object motion speed and direction directly onto NASA's opposed-flow and concurrent-flow wind-tunnel datasets, Flame Atlas turns static lab measurements into an interactive Safe Carry-Speed Simulator without requiring hours of supercomputer CFD computation.

* Ambient Intelligence Over Chatboxes: Instead of adding an isolated chat prompt, AI operates silently behind the controls—solving inverse design constraints, detecting nearby cliff-edge hazards, and narrating physics regime shifts automatically.

---

ENGINEERING FACTORS OUR TEAM CONSIDERED

* Microgravity Physics Fidelity: Strictly eliminated Earth-style buoyant flickering in $0g$, enforced dark standoff distances between fuel and reaction fronts, and flagged low-soot cool flames (ACME CFI-G) where standard optical cameras fail and radiometric/UV sensors are required.

* Human Survivability Guardrails: Constrained the Inverse Design Optimizer with minimum breathable oxygen partial pressures so the AI never recommends putting out a fire by rendering a crewed cabin unbreathable.

* Offline Demo Resilience & Latency: Decoupled the 60 FPS HTML5 Canvas requestAnimationFrame loop from React state re-renders and built a deterministic client-side physics fallback so the dashboard runs smoothly even without backend connectivity.

---

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, SOFTWARE & DATA USED

* Frontend: TypeScript, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, HTML5 Canvas 2D API (custom parametric flame and shaded planetary globe renderers), and Lucide Icons.

* Backend & Machine Learning: Python 3.11, FastAPI, Pydantic, NumPy, Pandas, and scikit-learn (Multi-Output Gaussian Process Regression with Matern + WhiteKernel covariance for predictive mean and standard deviation).

* NASA Datasets & Visual Assets:

- NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI): Normalized experimental tables, radiometer logs, color-ratio pyrometry profiles, and summary reports from PSI-25 (BASS-II), PSI-26 (BASS), PSI-62 (BASS Tomography), PSI-68 (FLEX-2), PSI-69 (FLEX), PSI-99 (SAFFIRE-II), PSI-102 (SAME), PSI-107 (SPICE), PSI-60 (SPICE Pyrometry), and PSI-159 (ACME CFI-G).

- NASA Planetary Imagery: Equirectangular surface maps from the NASA JPL Solar System Simulator and NASA SVS CGI Moon Kit.
